package_info.why_malicious: Not a malicious package, but running on deprecated Java 7 exposes the application to vulnerabilities in dependencies that can no longer be patched or upgraded, creating a significant security risk.

execution_context.file_location: transitive dependencies (various JARs loaded at runtime)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Use of outdated, vulnerable open source components due to inability to upgrade dependencies that require Java 8.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Allows exploitation of known vulnerabilities in dependencies that cannot be upgraded because the application is restricted to Java 7.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Running on an unsupported Java version prevents patching critical vulnerabilities in dependencies, leaving the application open to exploitation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior is to keep dependencies up to date and patch vulnerabilities. Here, the application is forced to use outdated, vulnerable libraries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legacy systems sometimes run on old Java versions for compatibility, but this is not recommended for internet-facing or critical infrastructure.
key_indicators: Inability to upgrade dependencies to non-vulnerable versions
Exposure to publicized CVEs in open source components

attack_chain.action: A vulnerability is disclosed in an open source dependency used by Nexus Repository Manager 2.x.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attackers become aware of the vulnerability.

attack_chain.action: Sonatype cannot upgrade the vulnerable dependency because the fix requires Java 8, but the application is running on Java 7.
attack_chain.leads_to: No patch is available for Java 7 users.

attack_chain.action: Attackers exploit the known vulnerability in the unpatched dependency.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromise of the Nexus Repository Manager instance.

behavioral_signatures: Application running on Java 7 with known-vulnerable dependencies
Inability to apply dependency upgrades due to Java version constraints
Presence of CVEs in loaded JARs
file_indicators: Outdated JAR files with known vulnerabilities in the lib/ directory
network_indicators: Unexpected outbound connections from vulnerable components (if exploited)
Indicators of compromise related to known CVEs in dependencies
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for applications running on Java 7, especially those with internet exposure. Scan loaded JARs for known CVEs. Flag any inability to upgrade dependencies due to Java version constraints as a critical risk. Use software composition analysis tools to identify and alert on vulnerable dependencies.
